questions.stem: Which of the following motions, if passed by the Lok Sabha, compels the Council of Ministers to resign immediately?
questions.explanation: A no-confidence motion — requires 50 members to support its introduction (Rule 198) — if passed, the Council of Ministers must resign (Art 75(3)). A censure motion expresses disapproval of a specific policy / action but does not compel resignation. Adjournment motion — discussion on a matter of urgent public importance, involves censure of the government but is not a no-confidence vote. Call-attention motion draws the government's notice to an urgent issue.

questions.stem: The first hour of every parliamentary sitting, devoted to oral questions to Ministers, is known as:
questions.explanation: Question Hour (11 AM to 12 noon) — questions to Ministers on matters of administration. Three kinds: starred (oral, green slip), unstarred (written, white slip), short-notice (pink slip). Zero Hour (12 noon to 1 PM) — an informal Indian innovation from 1962 — members raise matters of urgent public importance without prior notice (hence 'zero hour', the hour before lunch).

questions.stem: A 'Money Bill' in Indian Parliament can be introduced only in the:
questions.explanation: Art 109 — a Money Bill can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha, and with the prior recommendation of the President (Art 117). The Rajya Sabha has only a recommending role and must return the Bill within 14 days; the Lok Sabha may accept or reject its recommendations. The Speaker of the Lok Sabha decides whether a Bill is a Money Bill — and that decision is final (subject to judicial review since the 2023 Rojer Mathew judgment).

questions.stem: The quorum required for a sitting of either House of Parliament is:
questions.explanation: Art 100 — quorum for either House is 10 % of its total membership (including the Presiding Officer). So for Lok Sabha (545 members) quorum = 55; for Rajya Sabha (250 members maximum) quorum = 25. Below quorum, the Chair adjourns the House. The requirement has prevented rushed business in thinly-attended sittings.

questions.stem: A joint sitting of both Houses (Art 108) to resolve a deadlock on an ordinary Bill is presided over by the:
questions.explanation: Art 118 — the Speaker of the Lok Sabha presides over joint sittings of the two Houses. Joint sittings have been held only three times in India — Dowry Prohibition Bill (1961), Banking Service Commission (Repeal) Bill (1978), and the Prevention of Terrorism Bill / POTA (2002). Joint sittings are NOT held for Money Bills (the Rajya Sabha cannot block them anyway) or for Constitutional Amendment Bills (special majority required in both Houses separately).

questions.stem: The minimum age to be elected a member of the Rajya Sabha is:
questions.explanation: Art 84(b) — Rajya Sabha / Vidhan Parishad (Council of States / Legislative Council) members must be at least 30 years old. Lok Sabha / Vidhan Sabha — 25 years (Art 84(a) / 173). President / Vice-President / Governor — 35 years. Voter — 18 years.

questions.stem: If a member of Parliament remains absent from all sittings of the House for a period exceeding how many days, without permission, their seat becomes vacant?
questions.explanation: Art 101(4) — the seat of an MP becomes vacant if they are absent from all sittings of the House for 60 days without permission. The 60-day count excludes any period when the House is prorogued, adjourned for more than 4 days, or under recess. This provision ensures a minimum level of active participation.
